boardTitle: Unit Fractions: Partitioning, Naming, and Comparing
boardAcademicGoal: Students will understand that unit fractions represent one equal part of a whole divided into a given number of equal parts, and will use this understanding to compare unit fractions with different denominators.
coherence: Each node builds on the prior: students first establish that fractional parts must be equal in size, then apply this to identify and represent unit fractions (1/b) as one part of b equal parts, and finally reason about how the number of equal parts (denominator) affects the size of a single part, enabling comparison of unit fractions.

nodes.responsibility: Determine whether a shape has been divided into equal-sized parts, and divide given shapes into a specified number of equal parts.
nodes.academicBoundary: Limit to partitioning simple shapes (squares, rectangles, circles, bars) into 2, 3, 4, or 6 equal parts. Do not introduce fraction notation or naming of parts yet. Do not compare fractions or use denominators larger than 6.
nodes.evidenceGoal: Student correctly identifies equal vs. unequal partitions across at least 4 examples and correctly partitions at least 3 new shapes into a specified number of equal parts.

nodes.responsibility: Identify and represent a unit fraction (1/b) as exactly one of b equal parts of a whole, and connect the fraction symbol to the shaded/selected part.
nodes.academicBoundary: Restrict to unit fractions only (numerator of 1) with denominators 2 through 8. Do not address non-unit fractions (e.g., 2/3) or fraction comparison. Do not use improper fractions or mixed numbers.
nodes.evidenceGoal: Student correctly shades or selects one part matching a given unit fraction in at least 4 new examples (e.g., shape divided into fifths, sixths, eighths) and correctly writes the unit fraction for at least 3 shaded models.

nodes.responsibility: Compare two unit fractions with different denominators (e.g., 1/5 vs. 1/2) and justify which is larger based on the number of equal parts the whole is divided into.
nodes.academicBoundary: Limit to unit fraction comparisons only, using denominators 2 through 8, with same-size wholes. Do not introduce non-unit fraction comparisons, addition/subtraction of fractions, or equivalent fractions.
nodes.evidenceGoal: Student correctly compares at least 4 new pairs of unit fractions (using >, <, or =) and provides a correct reasoning statement (e.g., 'fewer equal parts means each part is bigger') for at least 3 of the comparisons.
